tools.name: resolve_place
tools.description: Find the Evendo ID of a country, region, city or neighbourhood by name. Always call this first: other tools take place IDs, not names. Names can be ambiguous (several 'Soho's), so check address_city / country_code in the results and pick the right one. If you don't know what kind of place it is, omi

tools.name: find_venues
tools.description: List venues of one type anywhere inside a place (country, region, city or neighbourhood), best-ranked first, or nearest-first when `near` is given; sort_by switches to highest rated, most reviewed or distance. Use for requests like 'top-rated cheap Italian restaurants in Prague', 'most reviewed bars

tools.name: search_venues
tools.description: Keyword search over venue names, taglines and descriptions (stemmed; 'brewery' matches 'breweries'; no typo tolerance). Scope it with within_place_id (from resolve_place) — never put the city name in the text. Short, concrete keywords work best: 'ramen', 'rooftop bar', 'flea market'. Combine with fi

tools.name: list_subareas
tools.description: List the direct children of a place, e.g. the neighbourhoods of a city or the cities of a region, most prominent first. Useful to suggest areas to explore or to narrow a search.

tools.name: get_venue
tools.description: Full details for one venue or place: description, address, coordinates, phone, website, booking link, photos, and all attribute tags. Pass the id from a previous result (or a slug like 'united-kingdom/london'). For several venues at once, use get_venues.

tools.name: get_venues
tools.description: Full details (same fields as get_venue) for up to 50 venues or places in one call, e.g. every stop of an itinerary. Pass ids and/or slugs from previous results; duplicates are fetched once. Results keep the order you passed (ids first, then slugs); anything not found is listed in not_found instead o
